senses.sense_definition: A waterproof overshoe worn over ordinary footwear to protect it from rain, mud, or snow.

examples.text: He slipped a rubber <w>galosh</w> over each dress shoe before stepping out into the sleet.
She took off each muddy <w>galosh</w> and left them on the porch.

senses.sense_definition: A waterproof rubber boot designed to be worn in wet or muddy conditions.

examples.text: He pulled on each tall <w>galosh</w> before heading out into the rainy garden.
Water seeped into his left <w>galosh</w> after he stepped into a deep puddle.

senses.sense_definition: A gaiter or protective legging covering the upper part of the shoe and part of the leg.

examples.text: The soldier fastened a leather <w>galosh</w> around his ankle to keep out dust.
Each vintage <w>galosh</w> was buckled tightly over his riding boots.

traits.comment: sense describing a gaiter or legging

senses.sense_definition: To walk while wearing, or as if wearing, galoshes; to splash or trudge through wet ground.

examples.text: The children were <w>galoshing</w> happily through every puddle along the road.
He spent the morning <w>galoshing</w> across the flooded fields to reach the barn.
